text:
maya: Quick question for the group: were finalizing the console flow for automatic fallback policies. Two things keep coming up in reviews: how intrusive should defaults be, and what minimal audit footprint do we ship so Support can root-cause without huge retention costs? Trying to pick safe defaults + an "operator-first" manual override.

alex: From runtime: defaults should be non-breaking. Id prefer Monitor -> Non-blocking fallback -> Block. Default to Monitor for 24h. Runtime needs these hooks: (a) window_secs (15/30/60), (b) consecutive_windows required to flip (hysteresis), (c) revert_backoff multiplier on repeated flaps.

nina: For supportability: every fallback event needs trace_id, route, policy_id, fallback_target, and a short error_code. Dont capture full prompts by default. Suggest baseline sampling 0.5% and an "investigate" button that temporarily pins 100% for a window and streams to Support UI.

jorge: UX suggestion: show a compact policy badge in the route table with a tooltip that summarizes: mode, threshold, sample rate, last_triggered_at. Clicking badge opens the policy drawer. Add an "escalate" action that triggers capture and notifies oncall.

maya: Good point on oncall. We should require "capture now" actions to include a rationale and be logged with actor id. Also need a per-customer billing flag when fallback switches model variants so customers know unit cost changed. Small note: prefer plain language labels: Observe, Route to fallback, Simplify response.

alex: Implementation caveat: when routing to cheaper models we must preserve token-level attribution in metrics. Add a billable_flag in fallback_event: "billed_variant": "yes/no", and surface delta in simulate. Also we should expose an operator hold that keeps the policy open for X mins to let humans debug.

nina: On audit retention: default aggregated counters should be kept long (90d), full-fidelity captures only on sample or capture-now (retain 7d). That balances investigations vs cost. Also add a per-policy retention override in enterprise plans.

jorge: Simulate idea: run policy against last 5m of aggregated telemetry and show "expected fallback rate", "expected extra tokens", and "estimated monthly cost impact". Put an inline risk score (low/med/high) based on how often the fallback target differs in latency/quality.

ops-bot: Policy preview created: preview/policy-1789 by @maya. Simulation job scheduled (low priority) id: sim-1789-045.

maya: Next steps: Alex will add hysteresis + revert backoff to the policy spec, Nina will write the audit retention defaults and capture-now UX, Jorge will prototype the badge/drawer flow, Ill combine copy for the three modes and the simulation summary. Well aim for a design pass tomorrow morning. Thanks. :rocket:

nina: One more ask  can the trace header include policy origin (ui vs api) and creator id? makes audits easier.

alex: yes, well add headers `X-RW-Policy-Id` and `X-RW-Policy-Origin` and include creator_id in policy metadata emitted with fallback events.

maya: perfect, closing this thread. Ill post mocks in #product when ready.
